$comment: Worker-class inventory for the swarm software factory — the classes the HARNESS itself ships, i.e. whose code lives in this repo. Read by the factory TUI's Fleet screen (tui/data/worker_classes.py); do not fork this data into a second table. Deliberately carries NO host names and NO product-specific workers: which machines run a class, and which extra classes a product repo runs, are per-deployment facts a consumer declares in its own worker-classes.local.json overlay beside its swarm-identity.sh (merged by id). Lock and marker paths are named by the LIB that owns them rather than repeated as literals, so this table cannot drift from the code it describes.
verified_against: docs/research/2026-08-15-factory-reengineering-survey.md#4 (worker inventory) — every field re-derived from the named source files, not copied from the survey's prose

classes.name: swarm worker
classes.trigger: cron 15,45 * * * *; issues:[labeled(ready-for-agent), closed]; workflow_dispatch; self-rearm dispatch when work remains and a worker ran
classes.lock: 2-slot host-capacity semaphore (host-capacity-lib.sh: slot 1 then slot 2, flock -n, yields if both busy); per-repo ready-set debounce stamp, 600s (schedule-lib.sh)
classes.writes: Forgejo labels/comments/close (close-report), git commits+push to main (or an agent PR under LANDING=pr), chat summary, swarm.db run/attempt/event rows, verdict file, runlog, materialised .env+secrets/, worktree/container sweep
classes.stuck_signal: verdict + runlog line on every exit; swarm.db unfinalised processes row = wedge evidence; explicit green-wedge detector (ready!=0, exit 0, zero worker-container births -> loud red + chat notice)
classes.invisible_failure_note: best-instrumented of the harness classes; not one of the survey's invisible classes

classes.name: triage
classes.lock: same 2-slot host-capacity semaphore as the swarm worker
classes.writes: Forgejo labels via claude -p /triage; issue comments/asks (post-issue-ask.sh); verdict file; chat digest of newly human-gated issues
classes.stuck_signal: trap 'verdict_write $?' EXIT; triage.yml's failure() step routes into the healer

classes.name: resume-asks
classes.trigger: cron 10,40 * * * * (offset from triage/swarm on purpose); workflow_dispatch
classes.lock: none — deliberately lockless, own shallow workdir disjoint from swarm/triage
classes.writes: Forgejo comment (durable ruling), label swap ready-for-human -> ready-for-agent, chat checkmark consuming the ask thread
classes.stuck_signal: resume-asks.yml's failure() step posts a direct chat alert naming the exact risk (parked issues not being re-armed)

classes.name: healer
classes.trigger: hourly cron (HEAL_MODE=watchdog, HEAL_DRY_RUN=1); also the failure() step of swarm.yml/triage.yml/ci.yml (HEAL_MODE=hook)
classes.lock: per-repo healer lock (flock -n, host-capacity-lib.sh's namespace), exits 0 if held
classes.writes: chat posts (ledger-gated), ledger files under $HEALER_STATE/<signature>, a per-repo evidence dir; HEAL_DRY_RUN=1 by default so no commits/pushes/tickets
classes.stuck_signal: none by design — healer.yml deliberately carries no failure() hook (self-failure must never recurse); a schedule of its own once silently deregistered for ~24h (2026-07-28) with zero alert until the storm the next day
classes.invisible_failure_note: one of the survey's explicitly named invisible-failure classes ("no run in Actions is the healer's only tell")

classes.name: reporter (rehearsal-report.sh)
classes.trigger: invoked by a consumer's rehearsal cycle on a red leg with a run dir, or directly by its box cleanup before teardown
classes.lock: none of its own — rides the caller's locks
classes.writes: new/appended rehearsal issues, priority label, native dependency wiring onto the drive issue, screenshot attach, comments; flips the drive to ready-for-human on filing failure; dispatches the swarm workflow; may delegate the first red leg to the rehearsal healer
classes.stuck_signal: none — set -uo pipefail (no -e) and every terminating path is an explicit exit 0 regardless of internal WARNs
classes.invisible_failure_note: one of the survey's explicitly named invisible-failure classes ("reporter... always exit 0")

classes.name: rehearsal healer
classes.trigger: called by the reporter's try_heal() for the first red leg only, gated REHEARSAL_HEALER=1 (default on)
classes.lock: none of its own — rides the caller's already-held locks; dedicated clone at $REHEARSAL_CHECKOUT, never the shared swarm checkout
classes.writes: at most one git commit pushed straight to origin/main, rails-enforced (<=3 files, <=60 lines, 1 commit, never the harness dir or the workflows); a heal-fail counter file per signature; a comment on the drive issue naming the fix
classes.stuck_signal: heal_fail_count (2 mechanical failures on one signature force filing) is the only self-limiter; bounded by a hard timeout; failures fold into the reporter's exit-0 umbrella
classes.invisible_failure_note: shares the reporter's exit-0 umbrella but is not itself one of the survey's named classes

classes.name: session-runner
classes.trigger: host cron; drains the ready-for-session queue (ADR 0174), one ticket per tick
classes.lock: own per-repo session-runner lock, plus joins the 2-slot host-capacity pool (host_capacity_acquire_heavy)
classes.writes: Forgejo agent-working/agent-blocked labels, issue comments, ticket state via its own headless claude session; chat notify(); local attempt-<n>/fail-<n> counters keyed per repo; per-run log file
classes.stuck_signal: thin — nearly every exit is exit 0 (including the two-strikes escalation path) and notify() degrades to a log-only line if chat is unreachable; it never appears in Forgejo Actions at all, so an identity-contract failure once flickered claims for ~15 ticks in silence
classes.invisible_failure_note: 100% exit-0, zero Actions visibility, notify() fails open — the best-evidenced candidate for the survey's unstated fourth invisible class

classes.name: schedule-backstop
classes.trigger: host cron; schedule-backstop.sh <workflow>.yml <window-min> — backstop for the 2026-07-28 silent-schedule-loss incident
classes.lock: none — stateless/idempotent, checks the Actions task listing each tick instead of holding a lock
classes.writes: dispatches the named workflow (POST /actions/workflows/<wf>/dispatches) when it decides a run is missing; no tracker/chat writes
classes.stuck_signal: none — fails closed silently on an API-listing failure (skip this tick); dispatch outcome logged to the cron log only, no chat either way
classes.invisible_failure_note: second-tier candidate surfaced by the same exit-code lens as the session-runner, but its failure mode is API-blip avoidance, not intentional success-masking

classes.name: in-run sweeps (janitor_sweep / claim-lib sweeps)
classes.trigger: automatic inside every run-swarm.sh execution: janitor_sweep() once at start; sweep_and_report() (reap_containers + sweep_worktrees) from the EXIT trap once SWEEP_ARMED is set
classes.lock: none of its own — piggybacks entirely on run-swarm.sh's already-held capacity slot
classes.writes: janitor_sweep: deletes stale swarm-claim comments + the agent-working label on issues whose claiming run died; sweep_and_report: force-removes stale worktrees (sparing any younger than a run lifetime), deletes only MERGED worker branches, and removes worker containers older than 3h
classes.stuck_signal: janitor_sweep || true swallows its own failure with zero alert — a broken janitor would silently strand tickets agent-working forever; the worktree sweep DOES warn on any unmerged branch it refused to delete
classes.invisible_failure_note: sub-step of the well-instrumented swarm worker, but janitor_sweep's own silent-failure swallow is worth flagging
